exceptions.rationale: The GC/1.3.2 translation unit must see declarations before code while retaining the same-owner object definitions at the tail. Moving definitions earlier changes text size, BSS size, register allocation, and exact-function count.
The retail translation unit sees four authoritative audio declarations but not the broad audio header. Including that header changes fn_1_2F22C by eight bytes.
The signed frandmod and rand8 declarations are target-backed local visibility. Broad random-function headers change five independently exact stage functions.

Retail shopevent.o omits the two weak sqrtf local statics emitted by generic math.h. Exact same-game board owners branch.c and player.c authenticate defining _MATH_H and including dolphin/math.h as the narrow translation-unit visibility pattern. The shopevent probe removes the 16-byte source-only prefix, makes all 11 paired functions and all selected relocation targets exact, and preserves every prior exact function.

The retained owner is byte-exact across .text, .rodata, .data, .bss, and 5,673 relocations. Address-unknown structure fields and explicit padding preserve target-backed sizes and consumer offsets without claiming semantics. The code_type pragmas are the authenticated source-chronology/link-order mechanism. One volatile-qualified model-ID load records the target's repeated reload of globally resident effect work across external calls; it is owner-specific evidence and does not authorize volatile register forcing elsewhere.

The complete GC/2.6 application owner is byte-exact only when the authenticated shared curve cluster and the two terminal tick functions retain separate code_type csects. File-qualified linker selectors concatenate .text, .text.common, and .text.after_common into the retail 0x366C order without changing any function body. The same-game w01Dll owner independently proves this source-chronology/link-order mechanism.

Retail indexes the 16-entry coinEffBankTbl with an unmasked mbRandMod(32), so indices 16-31 read the immediately adjacent coinEffBankTbl2. This is target-backed, not a decompilation error: mbCoinEffCreate at 0x8017C618 emits li r3,32; bl mbRandMod; addi r4,r28,0x150; lbzx r0,r4,r3 with r28 = 0x80247DE0, and symbols.txt gives coinEffBankTbl = .data:0x80247F30 size 0x10 with coinEffBankTbl2 at 0x80247F40. Both tables' retail bytes equal the source arrays. The adjacent in-range site uses li r3,16 against the equally sized coinEffColorNoTbl, proving the 32 is specific to this one call. Do not change the modulus to 16, mask or clamp the index, or merge the two tables.

SetObjAttrMotion initializes only attr, trans3D, rot and scale3D of a freshly allocated HU3D_ATTR_ANIM, leaving animId, texScrId, scale, trans, bitMapPtr and unk40 holding prior heap contents. Retail survives because the only dereference of Hu3DTexAnimData[animId] in hsfdraw.c FaceDraw sits on the right of an && whose left operand is the HU3D_ATTRANIM_ATTR_ANIM2D bit that this function clears; the preceding line takes the address only and never loads. Both game/hsfmotion.c and game/hsfdraw.c are Object(Matching), so both forms are retail-authenticated. Adding the missing initializers changes this object, and reordering or un-nesting FaceDraw's && changes that one.
